paper.title: Streptomyces shinuiensis sp. nov., a Salternamides-Producing Bacterium Isolated from Saltern Sediment
paper.licenseScope: Item page identifies open access under the article's Creative Commons Attribution license; article copyright is © 2025 authors. Article text and original material only; third-party items may have separate terms.

morphology.text: The type strain HK10T is described as aerobic, Gram-stain-positive and filamentous, with branched substrate mycelium and aerial hyphae bearing spore chains. The species account reports growth on ISP2 at 25–40 °C (optimum 30 °C), pH 7–9 (optimum 8), and 0–9% NaCl (optimum 3%).
morphology.locator: Species account, ‘Description of Streptomyces shinuiensis sp. nov.’
morphology.scope: Cultured type strain HK10T and stated laboratory media/conditions.

ecology.text: HK10T was isolated from saltern sediment on Shinui Island, Republic of Korea; the study identifies it as a producer of salternamides, with production context grounded in the cited prior isolation work.
ecology.locator: Abstract; Introduction; Materials and Methods, ‘Isolation and Strains’
ecology.scope: One cultured type strain and its reported collection context; no field ecological role inferred.

evolution.text: The authors place HK10T in Streptomyces using 16S rRNA and phylogenomic evidence, and report ANI and dDDH values below their cited species delineation thresholds against comparator type strains.
evolution.scope: The type strain and comparison set analyzed in this paper; authors’ taxonomic inference only.

distribution.text: The reported collection locality for HK10T is saltern sediment on Shinui Island, Republic of Korea.
distribution.locator: Abstract; Materials and Methods, ‘Isolation and Strains’; species account
distribution.scope: Single type-strain collection locality; no wider range implied.

paper.title: Pantoea graminicola sp. nov., a Gram-negative bacterium isolated from sweet corn (Zea mays L.) in the USA

paper.licenseScope: Publisher item page marks the paper Open Access and attributes copyright to authors; the Society's open-access licence form specifies CC BY 4.0. Article text and original material only; third-party items may have separate terms.

morphology.text: The paper characterizes the isolates as Gram-negative; the title and abstract report bacterial isolates KXB24, KXB25 and KXB45 from symptomatic sweet corn.
morphology.locator: Abstract; species description and phenotypic characterization
morphology.scope: The named cultured isolates and tested conditions only.

ecology.text: KXB24, KXB25 and KXB45 were recovered from symptomatic sweet corn in the Everglades Agricultural Area, Florida, USA; this source association does not establish causation or prevalence.

evolution.text: The authors use polyphasic taxonomic characterization, including genomic comparisons, to propose Pantoea graminicola for the studied isolates.
evolution.locator: Abstract; phylogenetic and genomic analyses; species description
evolution.scope: The isolates and comparator taxa analyzed in this treatment; authors’ taxonomic inference only.

distribution.text: The paper reports the studied isolates from symptomatic sweet corn in the Everglades Agricultural Area, Florida, USA.

paper.title: Genome-Based Reclassification of Two Haloarcula Species and Characterization of Haloarcula montana sp. nov.
paper.licenseScope: Article states open access under CC BY 4.0; article text and original material only; third-party items may have separate terms.

morphology.text: Cells of type strain GH36T are described as motile, pleomorphic irregular granules 1.0–4.0 μm and Gram-negative; colonies are red, elevated and round, about 0.5 mm in diameter.
morphology.locator: Results, phenotypic characterization; ‘Description of Haloarcula montana sp. nov.’
morphology.scope: Cultured type strain GH36T and stated assay conditions.

ecology.text: GH36T was isolated from a salt lake in China; this collection context alone does not establish ecosystem function or abundance.
ecology.scope: One cultured type strain and reported sample source.

evolution.text: The authors use genome-based comparisons and taxonomic characterization to propose Haloarcula montana for strain GH36T.
evolution.locator: Abstract; genome-based reclassification and phylogenetic analyses; species description
evolution.scope: The strain and comparator genomes analyzed in the 2025 study; authors’ taxonomic inference only.
